svg.aria-label: How to write 舞: 14 strokes · 13 pen lifts · 14 movements
svg.title: Writing 舞
svg.desc: 14 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 舞 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 舞.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E8%88%9E.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 舞, in three pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the top: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal, a longer horizontal under it, four short verticals from left to right, then a long horizontal across the whole width. Medians 9–11 draw 夕 as 外 opens: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a dot. Medians 12–14 draw the lower right: a horizontal, a short stroke that drops and turns right without lifting, then a long vertical down through them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
